{
  "participants": [
    {"login": "mercie-ux", "stance": "support", "note": "verified disk-space calculation discrepancy and tested"},
    {"login": "achow101", "stance": "objection", "note": "objected to converting internal units to GB, then ACKed when changed to GiB display strings"},
    {"login": "murchandamus", "stance": "support", "note": "ACKed alternative fix keeping GiB units"},
    {"login": "jeanpablojp", "stance": "support", "note": "tested pruned case on low disk volume"},
    {"login": "fanquake", "stance": "neutral", "note": "noted string and translation freeze timing constraints"},
    {"login": "hebasto", "stance": "objection", "note": "noted weirdness of GiB rounding with MiB prune granularity and GUI discrepancy, but found it acceptable for follow-up"}
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:5321049657",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Converting internal representations in chainparams to GB causes confusion with du defaults and reintroduces unit ambiguity",
      "quote": "Rather than changing the units that we use in the code, why not change the units as displayed to the user? ... As one of the people who do/review the chainparams updates, I strongly prefer to use GiB rather than GB since du uses the *iB units by default.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": ["c:5321406285"],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "c:5401547644",
      "settled_by_quote": "ACK 42215b85811a4950265fa2d02b22e83046ed95d5"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4005819331",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "Rounding prune sizes up to whole GiB produces confusing messages when prune is configured in MiB",
      "quote": "The -prune option has MiB granularity. It seems weird to specify -prune=550 and then see a message saying, \"Approximately 1 GiB of data will be stored in this directory.\"",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "r:5198448774",
      "settled_by_quote": "I think it's acceptable to keep \"GiB\" in the AppInitMain warning."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:5263166367",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "Traced chainparams math and verified a 63 GB discrepancy between the silent check and UI display",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4997891568",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "Approved the revised approach resolving the identified issue",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5382874487",
      "verdict": "Tested ACK",
      "reason": "Tested pruned case on a small volume, confirming -prune=550 warns 1 GiB instead of 856 GB",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5401547644",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "Approved the revision keeping internal units in GiB and updating strings",
      "substantive": true
    }
  ],
  "notes": "achow101's approach objection led the author to revise the PR to retain internal GiB units, which achow101 then ACKed. hebasto raised concern over GiB granularity for pruned nodes and noted intro.cpp inconsistencies, but concluded both were acceptable for now with the GUI being a follow-up."
}

participants.note: verified disk-space calculation discrepancy and tested

tested pruned case on low disk volume
noted string and translation freeze timing constraints
noted weirdness of GiB rounding with MiB prune granularity and GUI discrepancy, but found it acceptable for follow-up

claims.harm: Converting internal representations in chainparams to GB causes confusion with du defaults and reintroduces unit ambiguity
claims.quote: Rather than changing the units that we use in the code, why not change the units as displayed to the user? ... As one of the people who do/review the chainparams updates, I strongly prefer to use GiB rather than GB since du uses the *iB units by default.

claims.harm: Rounding prune sizes up to whole GiB produces confusing messages when prune is configured in MiB
claims.quote: The -prune option has MiB granularity. It seems weird to specify -prune=550 and then see a message saying, "Approximately 1 GiB of data will be stored in this directory."
claims.settled_by_quote: I think it's acceptable to keep "GiB" in the AppInitMain warning.

support.reason: Traced chainparams math and verified a 63 GB discrepancy between the silent check and UI display
Approved the revised approach resolving the identified issue
Tested pruned case on a small volume, confirming -prune=550 warns 1 GiB instead of 856 GB
Approved the revision keeping internal units in GiB and updating strings

result.notes: achow101's approach objection led the author to revise the PR to retain internal GiB units, which achow101 then ACKed. hebasto raised concern over GiB granularity for pruned nodes and noted intro.cpp inconsistencies, but concluded both were acceptable for now with the GUI being a follow-up.
